project: Free Shipping Supplies Directory - freebie sources for resellers

suppliers.name: USPS free branded boxes + envelopes
suppliers.cost: Free packaging; must ship Priority Mail / Priority Mail Express
suppliers.gist: Brand-new, service-branded boxes, flat-rate and padded envelopes, paks and pouches - shipped to your door free, or picked up at any Post Office counter.
details: Order from the Postal Store's 'Free Shipping Supplies' listing: singles, or packs of 10 and 25, shipped to you at no cost.
47 free products were listed in USPS's free-supplies filter as observed on 2026-11-02 - all Priority Mail or Priority Mail Express branded.
Key rule per USPS's own store text: 'Priority Mail Flat Rate shipping supplies may only be used to ship via Priority Mail Flat Rate' - service-branded supplies go with the matching service.
You pay postage as usual; the packaging itself is $0. Orders of 1-5 flat-rate items can be fulfilled by your local Post Office; bigger batches ship from distribution centers.
suppliers.url_label: USPS Postal Store - Free Shipping Supplies

price_evidence.claim: Free Shipping Supplies filter showed 47 items (Priority Mail 47, Priority Mail Express 11)
price_evidence.source: store.usps.com results page (bot-shielded to curl, content read via search snapshot)

price_evidence.claim: Supplies shipped to you at no cost; packs of 10/25; 'may only be used to ship via Priority Mail Flat Rate'
price_evidence.source: USPS store product page text (P_EP_14_F) in search snapshot

suppliers.name: USPS Flat Rate strategy (+ observed prices)
suppliers.cost: Free packaging; flat postage per type (prices observed)
suppliers.gist: Free flat-rate packaging with one fixed price regardless of weight (up to 70 lb) or distance - a winner for dense, heavy items shipping far.
details: Observed USPS-listed commercial prices on 2026-11-02: Flat Rate envelope $11.97; Legal envelope $12.51; Small Flat Rate box $12.95; Medium boxes $22.02 (retail $25.80); Large box $32.75 (retail $36.10); APO/FPO box $31.34.
Retail window pricing is higher - book postage online (Click-N-Ship or any discount platform) for commercial rates.
Flat Rate shines for heavy-to-far-zone lanes (book lots, tools, cast iron). It usually LOSES for light parcels vs. Ground Advantage tiers.
The Padded Flat Rate Envelope is the sleeper pick: clothing resellers can fill it generously and still pay the envelope price.

price_evidence.claim: FR envelope $11.97, legal $12.51, small box $12.95, medium $22.02/$25.80 retail, large $32.75/$36.10 retail, APO $31.34
Domestic rates are published in Notice 123 USPS guide; recheck after each USPS January price change

suppliers.name: USPS supply rules (reuse + misuse)
suppliers.cost: Free to follow - mistakes get expensive
suppliers.gist: 90 seconds of fine print that keeps you out of trouble: branded supplies ship the matching service, old labels die, and misuse is federal-law territory per USPS.
details: DMM 115 wording (Priority Mail Express): USPS-provided packaging 'must be used only for Priority Mail Express' - the same style of rule applies to Priority Mail packaging under DMM 135.
USPS's own FAQ on using and reusing boxes adds: 'Misuse may be a violation of federal law.'
Reusing USPS-branded boxes: allowed only for the matching service, and old labels/barcodes must be fully removed or blacked out.
Never put Priority-branded packaging under FedEx, UPS, or Ground Advantage postage; never resell or give supplies away as materials.
suppliers.url_label: USPS FAQ - Use or reuse boxes properly

price_evidence.claim: 'Misuse may be a violation of federal law' plus reuse guidance
DMM 115.1.1: USPS-provided Priority Mail Express packaging used only for Priority Mail Express

suppliers.name: USPS Ground Advantage - bring your own box
suppliers.cost: No free supplies; cheapest USPS lane for light parcels
suppliers.gist: The workhorse for 1-16 oz reseller parcels: weight-tier pricing, any sturdy box or mailer allowed, and no free branded supplies - pair it with the store give-aways and frugal picks below.
details: Observed 2026-11-02 on usps.com: Ground Advantage starts at $7.90 at the Post Office / $6.93 with commercial rates for the lightest tier.
Weight tiers step at 4 oz, 8 oz, 12 oz, and 15.999 oz - trimming cushioning (and using lighter mailers) can keep you in a cheaper tier.
Any plain, service-neutral box or poly/bubble mailer is acceptable; old labels must be removed or crossed out.

price_evidence.claim: Prices start at $7.90 at a Post Office / lower commercial rates; weight tiers 4/8/12/15.999 oz
price_evidence.source: usps.com Ground Advantage and business prices pages

suppliers.name: Post Office counters + free carrier pickup
suppliers.cost: Free
suppliers.gist: Supplies today? Ask the clerk. Parcels tomorrow? Your own carrier picks up prepaid boxes at your door - zero driving, zero spending.
details: Post Offices hand over Priority Mail sleeves, envelopes and boxes when you are shipping the matching service that day - ask politely; inventory varies by office.
USPS store text: local Post Offices can fulfill orders of 1-5 flat-rate supply items; larger orders ship from distribution centers.
Free Package Pickup: leave prepaid parcels for your regular carrier. USPS even ships your supplies order with a 'Carrier - Leave if No Response' endorsement.

price_evidence.claim: Local PO fulfills 1-5 flat-rate supply orders; supplies ship with 'Carrier - Leave if No Response' endorsement
price_evidence.source: store.usps.com product page text in search snapshot

suppliers.name: FedEx One Rate (free flat packaging)
suppliers.cost: Free packaging; flat rate per box/pak (prices vary by service)
suppliers.gist: FedEx's flat-rate program: pick eligible One Rate boxes or envelopes, they arrive free with your account, and the price is fixed by size.
details: One Rate requires its eligible packaging; grab it free online with a FedEx account or at a FedEx Office counter.
Observed 2026-11-02 on fedex.com: the FedEx 2Day flat rate for the One Rate envelope was $12.75 (other sizes and services differ).
If your item exceeds the packaging's size limits, FedEx re-rates it as a standard parcel - measure before you commit.

price_evidence.claim: FedEx 2Day flat rate: One Rate envelope $12.75; extras like Saturday delivery are additional fees

suppliers.name: FedEx free expedited packaging
suppliers.cost: Free with FedEx expedited / Express Saver / International Economy
suppliers.gist: FedEx says it plainly: shipping expedited? Envelopes, paks, poly bags, boxes and tubes are complimentary - order online and they ship them to you for free.
details: Per fedex.com: 'Complimentary FedEx packaging is only available for shipments using FedEx expedited, FedEx Express Saver or FedEx International Economy services.'
Free at FedEx Office and Ship Centers when you ship the same day; otherwise order with the free account.
FedEx Ground lanes (Ground, Ground Saver) want your own packaging - the freebies are the expedited family.

price_evidence.claim: Complimentary packaging scope (expedited, Express Saver, International Economy); free delivery of online orders

suppliers.name: UPS account supplies (order free online)
suppliers.cost: Free for account holders; supplies mainly fit express lanes
suppliers.gist: A free UPS profile opens their supplies ordering page: free UPS-branded boxes, envelopes and forms shipped to you in a few business days.
details: Per ups.com: 'UPS account holders get free UPS shipping supplies including packaging, forms and labels.'
UPS Ground requires your own boxes; the free packaging targets Next Day Air, 2nd Day Air, Worldwide Express and related express services.
The UPS Store counters hand out carrier supplies for single shipments processed there (per franchise store pages).

price_evidence.claim: 'UPS account holders get free UPS shipping supplies including packaging, forms and labels'

suppliers.name: The UPS Store counters (paid, varies)
suppliers.cost: Paid - prices set per franchise; call ahead
suppliers.gist: Franchise stores sell boxes, cushioning and mailers, and they pack for you - the paying escape hatch when one weird fragile item needs solving today.
details: Boxes from 6x6x6 up to 24x24x24, tubes, retention packaging, bubble cushioning, tape, markers, envelopes - DIY or their certified packers.
Prices differ between locations (independently owned); phoning your local store beats the website every time.

price_evidence.claim: Locator plus price policy: 'individually owned and operated, our prices may vary from other locations'
price_evidence.source: locations.theupsstore.com store pages via search snapshot

suppliers.name: DHL Express free packaging (international lanes)
suppliers.cost: Free with a DHL Express account (flyers free under 100 single-unit orders)
suppliers.gist: International buyer paid express? DHL account holders order free flyers, envelopes, boxes and tubes through their Online Supplies Order platform.
details: DHL OSO materials list boxes sized to 25 kg, tubes, card envelopes and poly flyers at 'No charge applied' for eligible account orders.
DHL note: DHL-branded packaging is not suitable for dangerous goods.
Rarely relevant for US-domestic e-commerce; keep it in your back pocket for cross-border heavyweights.

price_evidence.claim: Flyers/boxes/envelopes listed 'No charge applied'; Large Flyer free of charge for single-unit orders under 100 pieces
price_evidence.source: DHL OSO and MyDHL+ ordering pages (HTTP 200)

suppliers.name: Grocery + big-box produce/drink cases
suppliers.cost: Free - ask the stock manager
suppliers.gist: Banana boxes, egg flats and soda cases are free, sturdy, slotted, and they stack like bricks - the classic first fifty boxes for a new reseller.
details: Best picks: banana boxes (stable footprint, vented - line one with a fresh garbage bag), egg flats (built-in dividers), drink and produce cases.
Script that works: 'Hi! I ship packages - could I take some of those empty produce boxes off your hands?' Nearly everyone says yes.
Go after restock windows (early morning), offer to take a whole stack, and become a regular - stores like fewer bales to haul.
Wipe down and sniff test: bakery and produce boxes can carry odors into collectibles. Skip anything greasy, wet, or pest-scarred.

price_evidence.claim: Store-by-store practice; no official page to link. Phone first and ask for the stock manager.

suppliers.name: Bike shops (free cartons + foam)
suppliers.cost: Free boxes and foam inserts - call ahead
suppliers.gist: Bike boxes are the only free carton that safely ships a bicycle - and shops toss them weekly. Hit them after weekend sales rushes.
details: Wheel-and-frame sized cartons plus hub- and spoke-foam fittings - tall fragile pieces borrow this protection beautifully.
New-stock deliveries and weekend trades leave the biggest piles; Sunday evening or Monday morning pickup works best.
Bring something to bungee them down - these boxes are long and awkward.

price_evidence.claim: Store-by-store practice; no page to link. Phone first so they hold one behind the counter.

suppliers.name: Furniture, mattress + appliance stores
suppliers.cost: Free cardboard + foam protectors - ask at the dock
suppliers.gist: Warehouse staff slice huge clean cardboard sheets and stack foam corner blocks all day - often glad someone takes them instead of the baler.
details: Flat cardboard boards make instant picture-frame and glass-item protectors; foam corner blocks turn any plain box into a bumper system.
Ask for the loading dock or receiving manager, not the showroom floor - and offer to take everything they have noticed stacking up.
Appliance inserts and mattress-wrap sheets arrive clean and poly-wrapped in transit.

price_evidence.claim: Local dock policy; no link. Bring a bungee or tarp for the trunk.

suppliers.name: Liquor/wine store box dividers
suppliers.cost: Free 12-bottle boxes with dividers - call ahead
suppliers.gist: 12-slot dividers turn fragile shipments into neat modules - but mind the branding: ship these boxes inside-out or plain-paper covered.
details: The cardboard dividers are the prize: mugs, ornaments, salt shakers, small collectible figurines all ride perfectly.
If the box is printed with an alcohol brand, flip it inside-out or cover it with plain kraft - carriers treat alcohol-marked packaging as a flag, and USPS prohibits shipping alcohol entirely.
Ask for plain, unprinted cell-divider boxes first - most stores stock both styles.

price_evidence.claim: Local store policy; USPS rules prohibit shipping alcohol (branded packaging is a flag, not proof of license)
price_evidence.source: no link; USPS alcohol rules summarized in guide

suppliers.name: U-Haul 'Take a Box, Leave a Box'
suppliers.cost: Free exchange zone (where offered); new boxes from $2.04
suppliers.gist: U-Haul wants moving boxes reused: many neighborhood stores run a drop-off/take-free zone where movers swap boxes at no charge.
details: Leave your clean moving leftovers, take someone else's castoffs - a community recycle loop run by the store itself.
Not every location runs the exchange - check your local store page or call.
Observed at uhaul.com on 2026-11-02: new moving boxes 'as low as $2.04' - a decent nearby top-up (their $4.95 tape is in Frugal alternatives).

price_evidence.claim: Moving Box 'As low as: $2.04'; Supply Kit (5 boxes, 1 tape roll, 10 label pouches) $39.99

suppliers.name: Nextdoor free lists / FB Marketplace / Buy Nothing
suppliers.cost: Free (local groups + curb alerts)
suppliers.gist: Movers move out year-round, and 'free boxes' posts show up weekly - set saved alerts or someone else takes the stack in an hour.
details: Search free sections for 'boxes', 'moving boxes', 'bubble mailers'; set saved-search alerts so you respond while the pile is still there.
Apartment complexes: May and September are box monsoons - polite curb-picking near move-out weekends is a lifestyle.
Buy Nothing groups (hosted on Facebook) are hyper-local and generous by design; say thanks with a photo afterward.
Facebook marketplace links are login-gated to automated checks; Nextdoor's free board is the friendlier link.

price_evidence.claim: Community free listings (platform-dependent; login gates apply)
price_evidence.source: nextdoor.com (HTTP 200); facebook.com/marketplace returns 400 to bots - login-gated

suppliers.name: Office / school copy-paper cases
suppliers.cost: Free at any office, school or print room
suppliers.gist: Copy-paper cases are rigid, square, and free for the asking - the unglamorous MVP of heavy-part resellers.
details: Strong walls and tight lids make these ideal for tool kits, hardware, and dense collectibles that dislike flex.
Schools and offices unload them at end-of-year cleanouts; print shops and real-estate offices cycle them weekly.
Ask the receptionist or office manager; bring the empties back and they will happily refill your supply.

price_evidence.claim: Local office-surplus practice; no official page

suppliers.name: Level zero: reuse your own inbound packaging
suppliers.cost: $0 plus five minutes of label surgery
suppliers.gist: Every Amazon box and padded mailer you receive is reseller gold - if you strike the labels and match the lane.
details: Remove or fully black out old labels and barcodes - scanners can resurrect them and snarl tracking.
Service-branded inbound gets reused only for the same service (a Priority box only ships Priority again).
Plain brown boxes are open games for Ground Advantage and every ground courier.
Padded mailers usually keep their bubble intact; peeling a new outer label keeps them presentable.
Skip moldy, wet, or odd-smelling boxes - your five-star condition reputation starts at the bench.

price_evidence.claim: USPS FAQ covers reuse basics (old labels must be removed or obliterated)

suppliers.name: Cheap poly + bubble mailers (bulk math)
suppliers.gist: Mailers are the packaging you re-buy most, so the per-unit price matters: 100-count packs run $18-$20, while 1,000-count specialty cases drop to about 6 cents apiece.
details: Observed 2026-11-02: Staples 10x13 self-sealing 100/Box $19.99 ($0.20/mailer); Walmart StarBoxes 10x13 100 ct $18.40; USPACKSMART 12x15 100-pack from $13.29 to $20.85 by variant.
1,000-count cases observed: BulkMailerHQ 10x13 $54.99/1000 ($0.055 ea); Uline S-21878 1,000-case $194 ($0.19 ea).
Dollar Tree top-up ($1.25): Polyair XPAK individual poly mailer (12.5x18 usable) and Jot 6x9 bubble mailer - convenience pricing, not bulk.
Rule of thumb: poly for clothes, bubble mailers for glassware, rigid boxes for anything heavier than a paperback.

price_evidence.claim: Staples brand 10x13 poly mailer 100/Box $19.99 ($0.20/mailer)
price_evidence.source: staples.com product page in search snapshot

price_evidence.claim: Walmart StarBoxes 10x13 100-pack $18.40
price_evidence.source: walmart.com product page viewed via search snapshot

price_evidence.claim: BulkMailerHQ 10x13 1000-pack $54.99 ($0.055/mailer); Uline S-21878 1000-case $194

suppliers.name: Uline bulk boxes (real wholesale pricing)
suppliers.cost: $1.16/box for 12x12x12 at 25 qty - drops with volume
suppliers.gist: Uline sells at wholesale rates without a reseller license - the reliable per-box floor for serious volume, with same-day ship to boot.
details: Observed 2026-11-02: S-4125 (12x12x12, 200# test) at $1.16/box in the 25-bundle (orders in multiples of 25); the lighter 32-ECT version runs about $1.00/box.
Volume tiers drop the unit price further as quantity grows - plan around a 250-bundle if you ship weekly.
Watch Uline's shipping-sensitive minimum culture: one 25-bundle of small boxes keeps freight near-normal.
200# test vs 32 ECT explained: burst-strength vs edge-crush ratings; per Uline/UPS notes, 200# handles heavier loads (up to ~40 lb).

price_evidence.claim: S-4125 12x12x12 corrugated boxes 25/bundle at $1.16 each (multiples of 25)

suppliers.name: Packing tape: dollar stores vs bulk
suppliers.cost: $1.25-$1.50/roll at stores; ~$1.50/roll in bulk 18-packs
suppliers.gist: Mix a dollar-store emergency roll with a bulk pack and you are set for months - tape is the quiet subscription resellers never mean to buy.
details: Observed 2026-11-02: Dollar Tree Tool Bench clear packing tape $1.50; Jot 1.89" x 400" mailing tape $1.25 (a thin, short roll).
Observed 2026-11-02: U-Haul clear 55-yard shipping/packing tape $4.95; Amazon DowDew single 55-yd heavy-duty roll $4.49; Amazon JARLINK 18-roll pack $26.99 (~$1.50/roll).
Quick math: one 55-yard roll seals roughly 20-25 medium boxes; the ~$1.50/roll bulk tier is where resellers camp.
Comparison point from CBS (Aug 2026): Scotch 2-pack tape $1.25 at Dollar Tree vs $3.32 at Walmart.

price_evidence.claim: DT Tool Bench clear packing tape $1.50; Jot mailing tape (400 in) $1.25
U-Haul clear shipping/packing tape $4.95
Amazon JARLINK 18 rolls $26.99 (~$1.50/roll); DowDew single roll $4.49

suppliers.name: Newspaper printer roll ends (free void fill)
suppliers.cost: Free - ask the print room
suppliers.gist: Giant unprinted newsprint rolls sit free in newspaper print rooms - the cleanest void fill you will ever get, by the mile.
details: Unprinted means zero ink-transfer risk - safe next to collectibles and clothing alike.
Ask the press or production department at any local daily paper or commercial print shop - otherwise it gets baled for recycling.
One 24-inch-wide roll yields roughly 10-20 boxes worth of crumpled fill, and whatever scraps remain recycle cleanly.

price_evidence.claim: Local print-shop practice; no official listing exists

suppliers.name: Dollar Tree mailroom aisle ($1.25-$1.50 top-ups)
suppliers.cost: $1.25 per item (bubble mailer, cushion wrap, packing paper); tape $1.50
suppliers.gist: Fixed low prices beat big-box single-item buys when you are one roll short - but it is a convenience tier, not the bulk tier.
details: Observed 2026-11-02 (sameday.dollartree.com in-store prices): 12-in x 6-ft cushion wrap $1.25; Jot 6x9 bubble mailer $1.25; packing paper 20x20 (20 ct) $1.25; Polyair XPAK poly mailer $1.25; clear packing tape $1.50.
A $0.20-in-bulk poly mailer beats a $1.25 individual mailer every time - use Dollar Tree for emergencies and odd sizes.
The mailroom aisle exists in-store and on same-day order pages; the QR card below points at the collection.

price_evidence.claim: Cushion wrap $1.25; packing paper $1.25; bubble mailer $1.25; poly mailer $1.25; packing tape $1.50
price_evidence.source: sameday.dollartree.com mailroom collection and product pages (HTTP 200)

suppliers.name: Pirate Ship: free postage platform (the real cost-saver)
suppliers.cost: Free software; commercial USPS pricing + discounted UPS rates
suppliers.gist: No monthly fee, no per-label markup: commercial USPS pricing, discounted UPS rates, and Priority Mail Cubic priced below commercial.
details: Pirate Ship's own pitch: 'No monthly fees, markup or hidden costs' - the platform gets paid by carriers, not by you.
Priority Mail Cubic there is priced below commercial pricing - small dense packages (books, K-cups, electronic gadgets) get radical savings.
UPS Ground Saver and UPS flat-rate-style lanes live inside the same free account.
Where the free packaging stops helping (Ground lanes), smart postage platforms like this pick you back up.

price_evidence.claim: 'No monthly fees, markup or hidden costs'; Priority Mail Cubic below commercial pricing
